correctness.rationale: Unique canonical connected threshold words 0^(a1)1^(b1)... give s=max(b1-1+[a1=1],b2-1,...), t=a_last if b_last=1 else 0. The four disjoint one-block cases contribute R; for two or more blocks the first, interior and last blocks contribute U, geometric 1/(1-V), and W. Exact cumulative rational formula follows; n>=3 t=0 iff the word ends 11, while s=0 iff it starts 00 and has no adjacent 1s. Their counts are respectively 2^(n-3) and F_(n-2), with the first joint asymmetry at n=4. Independent direct graph verification for all canonical words through n=12 and 539 cumulative comparisons succeeded; finite checks are not substituted for proof. The K2 boundary is handled (s=t=1).

originality.rationale: The global joint symmetry theorem (Fürnsinn–Gangl–Rubey) and its chordal refinement do not imply symmetry in the smaller threshold subclass, and in fact this subclass has a provably asymmetric joint distribution. The unique canonical binary encoding is previously known and explicitly credited. The new claim is a complete rational bounded-statistic census together with the sharp first symmetry failure and Fibonacci-versus-exponential marginal defect. The inspected specialist threshold-graph literature and closest mathematical records do not state an equivalent joint census. Priority remains provisional because literature searches cannot exclude unindexed work.

value.rationale: A recent symmetric joint law for sibling and tuft statistics holds even on chordal graphs; determining a natural structural boundary of that phenomenon is directly motivated. Connected threshold graphs are a canonical strict hereditary subclass with unique binary coding. Rather than reporting only a four-vertex counterexample, the theorem supplies a complete parameter-wise rational joint enumerator, proves the first failure is exactly four vertices, and quantitatively identifies the exponential marginal asymmetry (2^(n-3) versus Fibonacci). The exact enumeration provides reusable graph-class statistics, not a renamed known graph count.
